thread.title: Market Update: Sept. 26, 2018

author: Emily McCormick
title: Market Update: Sept. 26, 2018
text:
U.S. stocks held onto small gains at market open Wednesday ahead of the announcement of the Federal Reserve’s latest monetary policy decision.
The S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose 0.1%, or 2.95 points, while the Dow ( ^DJI ) rose 0.06%, or 17.21 points at 9:36 a.m. in New York on Wednesday. The Nasdaq ( ^IXIC ) rose 0.18%, or 15.86 points.
Experts largely agree that the central bank will raise interest rates a quarter point to between 2% and 2.25%, which would represent the highest level in more than a decade. If the Fed raises its benchmark interest rate as expected, it would mark the third rate hike this year. Many analysts also expect the Fed to raise rates a fourth time this year in December. Yields for the benchmark 10-year Treasury note hovered around 3.08 percent.
The Fed’s economic projections Wednesday will also detail the central bank’s economic forecasts for 2021.
ECONOMY: Fed’s latest decision looms The Fed’s decision will be released at 2 p.m. Wednesday , with Fed Chairman Jerome Powell set to speak in a press conference 30 minutes following the release. Analysts expect that he will be questioned about the impacts of continuing trade tensions on the economy — which the Fed had not referenced in its policy statement from Aug. 1 — as well as his thoughts on raising interest rates above the neutral rate and the balance sheet runoff.
“We do not expect any major changes to officials’ characterization of current U.S. economic performance, nor any major changes to the current stance of monetary policy, ‘accommodative,’ nor to the forward guidance,” Sam Bullard, managing director and senior economist for Wells Fargo Securities, wrote in a note ahead of the announcement. “While growth prospects remain favorable, uncertainty over trade policy will likely keep the risks to the economic outlook as ‘roughly balanced.’”
Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell testifies before a House Financial Services Committee hearing on the “Semiannual Monetary Policy Report to Congress,” at the Rayburn House Office Building in Washington, U.S., July 18, 2018. REUTERS/Mary F. Calvert/File Photo More Sales of new single-family U.S. homes rose 3.5% in August to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 629,000, the Commerce Department said in a statement Wednesday , buoyed by surges in purchases of new homes in the Northeast and West. The results narrowly missed expectations of 630,000, according to data compiled by Bloomberg, and July’s rate was downwardly revised to 608,000.
“The economy is strong. Labor markets are solid,” IHS Markit’s Patrick Newport said. “Yet, new home sales and single-family housing starts and permits have stalled. How can this be? Part of it is affordability. The 30-year mortgage rate has climbed about 65 basis points this year and is currently at levels last seen in May 2011; home prices as measured by the Federal Finance Housing Agency (FHFA) were higher in all 50 states in the second quarter from a year earlier; lumber prices in the summer were at an all-time high; and the tariffs on steel, aluminum and Canadian Softwood Lumber have raised the costs of building. This has choked off demand. On the supply side, rising construction costs, a lack of buildable lots, and a shortage of skilled labor have reduced incentives to build new homes.”
NEWS: Fox to sell Sky shares to Comcast, big tech heads to Washington, D.C. Fox ( FOX ) will sell its 39% stake in Sky ( SKY.L ) to Comcast ( CMCSA ), just days after Comcast won an auction to purchase the European media company with a $40 billion bid. Disney ( DIS ), which will soon be the parent company to Fox, consented to the deal, according to a statement. Fox’s Sky stake is valued at more than $15 billion.
Major tech companies including AT&T ( T ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), Twitter (TWTR ), Apple ( AAPL ) and Charter ( CHTR ) will discuss data privacy in testimony Wednesday before the Senate Commerce Committee . Consumer privacy has been a major debate between the tech community and lawmakers this year, with California passing the country’s first privacy bill over the summer.
